extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NIH grants and NIH review staff/administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how NIH Center for Scientific Review (CSR) organizes grant application review: the role of Review Branches and the different types of study sections/Special Emphasis Panels that evaluate applications. Useful for applicants understanding where and how their application will be assigned and for administrators assigning reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to Review Branch then Study Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications generally are assigned first to an RB, and then to a specific study section within that RB for evaluation of scientific merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Assisted Referral Tool. This describes the procedural workflow: initial assignment at the Review Branch (RB) level followed by placement into a specific study section (Scientific Review Group, SRG) for peer review of scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Branches (RBs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review activities of the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) are organized into Review Branches (RBs). Each RB represents a cluster of study sections around a general scientific area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RBs group related study sections by scientific discipline and serve as the first level of assignment for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chartered Study Sections (regular/temporary members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chartered study sections: Reviews most investigator-initiated research applications (R01, R03, R21, R15, and Ks). Chartered study sections are those with both regular and temporary members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the typical membership structure (regular + temporary members) and the common application mechanisms reviewed (R01, R03, R21, R15, K-series).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Study Sections (recurring SEPs, temporary members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Business Innovation Research and Technology Transfer Research Study Sections: Recurring special emphasis panels (SEPs) review Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Technology Transfer Research applications (STTR). They include only temporary members, recruited based on expertise needed for each meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recurring SEPs focused on SBIR/STTR mechanisms; membership is entirely temporary and tailored to the expertise required for that meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Study Sections (recurring SEPs for F-series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship Study Sections: Recurring special emphasis panels (SEPs) review individual fellowship grant applications - F30, F31, F32, F33. Temporary members are recruited based on expertise needed for each meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship applications (F-series) are typically reviewed by recurring SEPs composed of temporary members selected for relevant fellowship expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other CSR Study Sections / Special Emphasis Panels (one-time or recurring for special topics/conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Other CSR Study Sections (Special Emphasis Panel): Other one-time or recurring Special Emphasis Panels (SEPs) are held to review applications on special topics and members conflict applications. They include only temporary members, recruited based on expertise needed for each meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEPs can be convened either once or recurring to handle special-topic reviews or conflict-of-interest cases; membership is temporary and expertise-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV/AIDS-related applications expedited review
rubrics_metrics.description: HIV/AIDS Research: HIV/AIDS-related grant applications are reviewed on an expedited cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a procedural prioritization: applications related to HIV/AIDS are placed on a faster/exedited review timeline (no further detail provided on exact timing).
